phase2.conclusion: future topology prediction significantly improves scheduling (-7.9% vs no-future; -6.0% vs legacy provider); direct resource substitution significantly harms; oracle gap remains 14.7%

phase3.corrected_conclusion: scheduling gain is driven by predicted future-length/termination (early-stop) structure; content is not superior to legacy when shape-matched; resource adds nothing at H=5; largest remaining headroom is horizon
phase3.zero_length_check: pred=0 => P(actual<=1)=0.999; pred>0 => P(actual=0)=0.000; actual=0 => 100% caught

phase4.conclusion: content identity has no positive scheduling value (oracle content is worse); consuming q(A) as expected cost gives a small gain vs top-1 but loses to lane averages; length/survival remains the only main value; resource adds nothing at H=5

phase5.conclusion: H=10 saturates the horizon gap (10.2s over H5; H20 = H10); risk-sensitive consumption of predicted quantiles converts (-10.5s vs E2); identity costs remain harmful (lane-average still 1.8s better than risk)

phase7a.conclusion: scenario+CVaR beats E2 but loses to summed p95; q95 confirmed on frozen confirm300; comonotone and higher kappa do not help (penalty shape, not conservatism magnitude); kappa=0 worse than E2

phase7bc.conclusion: no consumer beats q95; adaptive risk helps only with a queue-pressure term and still loses; component split shows the entire gain comes from the runtime tail (rt95 == q95), load-tail weighting is harmful
